name: MassMIND
summary: Long-wave infrared image dataset of a harbour environment with semantic and instance segmentation masks for maritime scene understanding.
why_it_matters: Thermal perception is what keeps an autonomous surface vessel aware of obstacles at night and in haze, when RGB fails.
hackathon_notes: Download the three Google Drive zips in the README (2,916 LWIR images at 640x512, 7 classes, semantic and instance masks); small enough to fine-tune a segmentation net in a few hours. Licence is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 - non-commercial only.

name: LaRS evaluator
summary: Evaluation scripts for LaRS, a panoptic maritime obstacle detection benchmark spanning lakes, rivers and seas.
why_it_matters: Gives a standard scoring harness for USV obstacle detection so a team can compare its model against published baselines.
hackathon_notes: Pair with the LaRS dataset from the project page (4,000+ labelled key frames; test GT is hidden, so score test predictions on macvi.org); use the evaluator to score a YOLO/segmentation baseline. Dataset terms: CC BY-NC 4.0, research access only, no commercial use, no sharing images with third parties. The evaluator repo has no licence file.

name: SubPipe
summary: Underwater dataset recorded by a lightweight AUV inspecting a submarine pipeline: two cameras, side-scan sonar (10,030 images, COCO/YOLO labels), segmentation masks and navigation data, for segmentation, detection and visual-inertial localization.
why_it_matters: One of few open AUV datasets with a pose reference (estimated from the vehicle's own navigation sensors, not an external ground truth), useful for testing underwater VIO where GNSS never reaches.
hackathon_notes: Full set is ~80 GB unzipped on Zenodo; start with SubPipeMini (~12 GB) and run an off-the-shelf VIO to show drift underwater. Data CC BY 4.0, repo code GPL-3.0.

name: CART - Caltech Aerial RGB-Thermal
summary: Aerial RGB plus thermal dataset from natural terrain (rivers, coasts, deserts, forests) with GPS and inertial data, plus benchmarks for segmentation, RGB-to-thermal translation and VIO.
why_it_matters: Thermal-aerial data with GPS/IMU is rare; it supports night-time visual and thermal navigation research without flying your own sensor rig.
hackathon_notes: Use the VIO benchmark to test thermal-inertial odometry, or train RGB-to-thermal translation to build synthetic thermal maps. The labelled subset downloads directly; raw data are ROS1 bags from an S3 bucket. Non-commercial only: data.caltech.edu lists CC BY-NC 4.0 (README says CC BY-SA 4.0, non-commercial).

name: Drone-vs-Bird Detection Challenge
summary: Repository of the long-running Drone-vs-Bird challenge: annotations and instructions for a video dataset of small drones with birds as distractors.
why_it_matters: Telling a distant drone from a bird is the core false-alarm problem in camera-based C-UAS; this is the reference benchmark.
hackathon_notes: Videos only on request (wosdetc@googlegroups.com) after signing a data usage agreement, research use only - allow lead time. Then train a small-object YOLO; the hard part is tiny targets, so tile the frames. Repo not updated since 2022-12 (2023 edition is the last listed).

name: DroneAudioDataset
summary: Indoor recordings of drone propeller noise augmented with noise clips, organised for binary and multiclass audio drone detection.
why_it_matters: A common baseline audio set for acoustic drone detection. Note: its licence explicitly forbids military/defence use, so check fit before building on it.
hackathon_notes: Licence allows educational and non-commercial academic research only, and explicitly bans military, defence, intelligence, security and surveillance use - not usable for a defence entry; pick another acoustic set. The 'Unknown' clips come from ESC-50 and Speech Commands under their own licences.

name: Drone detection dataset (IR, visible, audio)
summary: Multi-sensor dataset from a Swedish thesis: 650 infrared and visible videos (airplane, bird, drone, helicopter; 203k labelled frames) plus 90 audio clips (drone, helicopter, background).
why_it_matters: Lets a team prototype sensor fusion for C-UAS (thermal + RGB + audio) on one consistent set of targets and distractors.
hackathon_notes: Data sits in the repo (~360 MB, no LFS), CC0. Labels are MATLAB groundTruth .mat files that scipy cannot read; use pip install mcos-decoder in Python. Good for a fused IR+audio classifier demo in a weekend.

name: RF-Drone-Detection (Georgia Tech)
summary: Georgia Tech student project on passive RF drone detection: a wifi_monitor.py script that flags DJI MAC OUI prefixes via airodump-ng, plus hackrf_sweep and GNU Radio experiment tools.
why_it_matters: Shows a cheap passive RF detection path for drones that use Wi-Fi links.
hackathon_notes: Needs root and a monitor-mode Wi-Fi adapter (tested on 2.4 GHz only, Ubuntu 18.04). It only matches two DJI OUI prefixes, so it misses non-Wi-Fi links and is trivially spoofed. No licence file.

name: Noisy Drone RF Signal Classification
summary: Loader and inspection scripts for a Kaggle drone RF benchmark: 16,384-sample IQ vectors and spectrograms from 6 drone remote-control transmitters plus a noise class, at SNR -20 to 30 dB in 2 dB steps.
why_it_matters: SNR-labelled RF samples let you measure how a drone RF classifier degrades with distance and noise.
hackathon_notes: Kaggle download is ~26 GB (CC BY 4.0; repo code GPL-3.0). Load dataset.pt with the provided PyTorch dataloader, then train a small CNN.

name: RFClassification
summary: Notebooks that classify drone presence and type from RF using DroneRF and DroneDetect data (PSD+SVM and CNN approaches), aiming at real-time use with GamutRF hardware.
why_it_matters: Ready-made baselines on the two most-cited public drone RF datasets.
hackathon_notes: Fork of the archived IQTLabs/RFClassification; no commits since 2022-09. Includes Raspberry Pi 4 test scripts. Download DroneRF (Mendeley, CC BY 4.0) and DroneDetect (IEEE DataPort, CC BY 4.0, 65.8 GB, needs an IEEE account) separately.

name: Drone Detection and Identification using RF signals
summary: Notebooks and MATLAB feature extractors for drone detection and identification on DroneRF: PSD, MFCC and time-domain features with XGBoost, a 1D-CNN and a CNN+XGBoost hybrid.
why_it_matters: Another reproducible baseline on public drone RF data to compare against.
hackathon_notes: Notebook-based; the processed data is on the Google Drive link in the README, raw DroneRF is CC BY 4.0 on Mendeley. Feature extraction scripts need MATLAB.

name: CNN for drone detection using RF
summary: CNN code for drone detection and identification on RF spectra.
why_it_matters: Simple CNN baseline for RF drone ID.
hackathon_notes: Older code (2020): three Keras scripts that read DroneRF's RF_Data.csv and use the old keras.layers.core API; use as reference only.

name: GNSS jamming/spoofing classification notebooks
summary: Colab notebooks for GNSS jamming-type classification (ML, DL and CV on spectrogram images) from a public raw-IQ jamming set, plus one GPS spoofing ML notebook; companion to arXiv 2501.02352.
why_it_matters: Turnkey starting point for a jamming-type classifier using open data.
hackathon_notes: Open in Colab and download the Zenodo IQ set (1.9 GB, CC BY 4.0). Its signals are simulated in MATLAB: DME, narrowband, AM, chirp, FM and no jamming. The repo has no licence file.

name: Towards Jammer Fingerprinting
summary: LSTM (Bayesian and standard) classifiers that identify individual jammers from IQ recordings, from an ICL-GNSS 2024 paper on how environment and receiver affect classification.
why_it_matters: Fingerprinting which jammer is present is a step toward attribution and targeted mitigation.
hackathon_notes: Needs your own IQ recordings in the expected file layout; reuse the model code on Jammertest data.

name: Sentinel-1 RFI detection
summary: Pipeline that flags radio-frequency interference in Sentinel-1 C-band SAR scenes using temporal z-scores and DEM slope masking, run over Iran, the Persian Gulf and Jammertest 2025.
why_it_matters: Free satellite data as a wide-area RFI sensor, complementing ADS-B based maps - but Sentinel-1 is C-band, and the authors' own Jammertest analysis could not tie detections to L-band GNSS jammers.
hackathon_notes: Needs a free Copernicus Data Space account. Pull Sentinel-1 scenes for a region and produce an RFI heatmap; present it as an RFI map, not a proven jamming map. MIT.

name: foxhunt
summary: Receive-only GNSS interference detection with radio direction finding and triangulation on Raspberry Pi and RTL-SDR.
why_it_matters: Low-cost jammer localization is a practical defensive EW capability.
hackathon_notes: Needs 3+ Raspberry Pi + RTL-SDR nodes with directional antennas; start with foxhunt-sim and --mock-sdr after uv sync. Receive-only, but a live test still needs an authorised interference source. Rotator GPIO driver and PPS wiring are still planned.

name: geoveil-cn0
summary: Rust library with a Python API (pip install geoveil-cn0) that scores GNSS signal quality from RINEX observation files via C/N0 and flags jamming, spoofing and interference across six constellations.
why_it_matters: Drop-in signal-quality monitor for a navigation stack.
hackathon_notes: Input is plain RINEX 2-4 files (decompress Hatanaka first); the spoofing check needs a broadcast nav file. Licence is PolyForm Noncommercial with an attribution term - no commercial use.

name: GNSS multiple jammers dataset
summary: Placeholder repo: its description promises recordings of several simultaneous chirp jammers on GPS L1 for notch-filter (ANF) mitigation studies, but the repo is empty (no commits) as of 2026-11-06.
why_it_matters: Multi-jammer data is rare; useful for testing mitigation filters.
hackathon_notes: No data, README or licence yet - nothing to use. Watch the repo or pick another jamming set.

name: GNSS jamming detection on maritime Antarctica dataset
summary: Thesis code for ML jamming detection and temporal generalisation using real maritime receiver diagnostics (u-blox MON-RF, MON-SPAN, RXM-MEASX) from a public Antarctica voyage dataset.
why_it_matters: Uses receiver-reported diagnostics a cheap u-blox already exposes, so it transfers to real hardware.
hackathon_notes: The Antarctica UBX set is one 45.7 GB zip on Zenodo (CC BY 4.0). Labels are the receiver's own jamming flag and the thesis results are a two-day pilot. Reproduce on your own u-blox logs by enabling the same UBX messages. Repo has no licence file.

name: P-D defense
summary: MATLAB implementation of the power-distortion detector for GNSS spoofing and jamming.
why_it_matters: Classic signal-level spoofing detector from the Humphreys line of work.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2020; read alongside the TEXBAT data.

name: Stanford GNSS spoof detection
summary: A single MATLAB script (DoAsimulationStudy.m) simulating direction-of-arrival spoof detection, supporting Rothmaier et al. Stanford GPS Lab papers.
why_it_matters: Reference implementations of spoofing detection tests.
hackathon_notes: Old MATLAB, one simulation script; useful only as an algorithm reference for DoA-based spoof detection.

name: GPS-Spoofing-Detect
summary: MATLAB course project with a write-up that tests GNSS spoofing detection on the TEXBAT DS7 scenario, with its own IQ extraction and least-squares navigation code.
why_it_matters: Small educational example.
hackathon_notes: Reference only. Needs TEXBAT processed data (open index on rnl-data.ae.utexas.edu, no terms stated) and spanikp's GNSS-toolbox. No licence file.

name: NRC UAV vs bird radar tracks
summary: Labelled real-world radar tracks of small UAVs, birds, humans and vehicles from an Echodyne EchoGuard radar over several Canadian field trials.
why_it_matters: Radar track classification (drone vs bird) is central to C-UAS beyond micro-Doppler range; open labelled radar data is scarce.
hackathon_notes: Train a kinematic-feature classifier on the tracks; no RF hardware needed.

name: MMC-UAV dataset
summary: Placeholder for a multimodal low-altitude anti-drone dataset (RGB, infrared, active radar, passive RF); the repo holds only a 3-line README that calls it MMA-UAV.
why_it_matters: Rare dataset with all four C-UAS sensor modalities.
hackathon_notes: No data, download link, paper or licence in the repo - not usable until the authors publish.

name: Audio localization dataset (Crazyflie)
summary: Datasets for acoustic echolocation and sound-source localization recorded on a Crazyflie drone and an e-puck robot.
why_it_matters: Shows acoustic sensing as a localization modality on micro drones.
hackathon_notes: Niche; useful if exploring acoustic self-localization.

name: Batear datasets
summary: Small Git LFS collection of drone and background audio for ESP32-S3 acoustic detection: about 89 WAV clips of DJI Mavic Pro, Mini 4 Pro and 5-inch FPV flights, ambient (urban, rural, fireworks, bat sites) and synthetic sweeps, plus resample and spectrogram tools.
why_it_matters: Targets low-cost acoustic sensor nodes - the cheapest C-UAS tripwire.
hackathon_notes: MIT. Run git lfs pull to get the audio. Pair with the Batear firmware for a microcontroller acoustic sensor demo.

name: drone-acoustic-detection
summary: Open field-test toolkit for acoustic and radar detection of low-signature drones on COTS hardware, aiming at FPV detection baselines.
why_it_matters: FPV-class detection baselines are missing in literature; this gives a reproducible method.
hackathon_notes: MIT, but the README frames it as research and educational use. No field recordings ship in the repo - the experiments run on synthesized signals (--mock) until you record your own. Follow the field protocol to measure your own detection ranges.

name: Game4Loc / GTA-UAV
summary: Benchmark and code for UAV geo-localization trained on synthetic game imagery with partial-match drone-satellite pairs (AAAI 2025).
why_it_matters: Synthetic data generation for geo-localization reduces the need for real flight data.
hackathon_notes: Code Apache-2.0; the HF dataset cards also say Apache-2.0, but the imagery is rendered from GTA V, so check the game's terms before non-research use. LR set 12.8 GB, HR 143.3 GB. Pretrained cross-area and same-area checkpoints on HF; fine-tune on your area's satellite tiles.

name: PiLoT
summary: Neural pixel-to-3D registration for UAV ego-localization and target geo-localization against a geo-referenced 3D map; release uses 3D Gaussian Splatting map backends (CVPR 2026).
why_it_matters: Absolute 6-DoF pose from a 3D map is a strong GNSS-denied fix for low-altitude drones.
hackathon_notes: GPU-heavy (CUDA extension build, CityGaussian conda env); demo data is about 15 GB. Code is MIT, but PiLoT-data on HF is gated: non-commercial research or education only, no redistribution. From NUDT, which is on the US Entity List - check your programme's rules.

name: FSRA
summary: Transformer-based feature segmentation and region alignment for drone-to-satellite geo-localization (TCSVT 2022).
why_it_matters: Widely used baseline on University-1652.
hackathon_notes: No licence file (all rights reserved). Trains on University-1652, which is request-only and research use only. Good comparison baseline.

name: PairUAV
summary: Baseline for last-meter UAV navigation using diffusion-refined aerial visual servoing; serves as the baseline for the ACM MM 2026 UAV workshop challenge.
why_it_matters: Moves geo-localization from retrieval to precise relative positioning for the final approach.
hackathon_notes: No licence on the repo. Training needs University-1652 (request-only, research use only), and the bundled SuperGlue code is Magic Leap's non-commercial research-only code. Competition test set is on HF; official scores only via CodaBench.

name: UAVM 2023 challenge
summary: Page for the ACM MM 2023 drone-satellite matching challenge on University-160k, listing team code repos and the leaderboard.
why_it_matters: Index of open winning-team code for drone-satellite matching.
hackathon_notes: Public entries: MLPN (4th, R@1 92.77), DPN (6th, 90.02) and BingY998 (7th, 85.76); the top two are private, and MBEG's 98.94 was removed for using University-1652 test data. Data is University-1652-derived (request-only, research use).

name: UAVM 2024 challenge
summary: Page for the ACM MM 2024 multi-weather drone-satellite matching challenge, listing team repos.
why_it_matters: Adds weather robustness to cross-view geo-localization.
hackathon_notes: Only two listed entries are public: WAGL (4th, R@1 94.07) and WELN (5th, 85.58). Challenge data (University160k-WX) builds on University-1652 (request-only, research use).

name: MuseNet
summary: Multiple-environment self-adaptive network for aerial-view geo-localization under varied weather (Pattern Recognition 2024).
why_it_matters: Weather robustness for drone-satellite matching.
hackathon_notes: MIT code; needs University-1652 (request-only, research use). Its University-WX weather augmentation matches the UAVM 2024 multi-weather setting, but it is not named as the official challenge baseline.

name: WELN
summary: Siamese-network solution to the ACM MM 2024 multi-environment drone-satellite matching challenge.
why_it_matters: Open challenge entry for weather-robust geo-localization.
hackathon_notes: No licence (all rights reserved). Weights and the University1652-Plus weather set are on Baidu pan only, may be hard to fetch; the data derives from University-1652 (research use). 5th on the public leaderboard (R@1 85.58), 4th after one team was removed.

name: MLPN (UAVM 2023 entry)
summary: Team solution for the ACM MM 2023 drone-satellite matching challenge, 4th on the leaderboard (R@1 92.77).
why_it_matters: Open challenge entry.
hackathon_notes: MIT. Training script with hard-coded paths; needs University-1652 (request-only, research use).

name: DPN (UAVM 2023 entry)
summary: Submission for the ACM MM 2023 drone-satellite matching challenge.
why_it_matters: Open challenge entry.
hackathon_notes: One-line README, no licence (all rights reserved). 6th on the UAVM 2023 leaderboard (R@1 90.02). Needs University-1652 (request-only, research use).

name: MBEG
summary: Modern-backbone efficient geo-localization solution for UAVM 2023 including distillation training.
why_it_matters: Open entry with distillation, useful for edge deployment.
hackathon_notes: MIT. Topped the leaderboard (R@1 98.94) but was removed for using University-1652 test data; the method and distillation code are still useful. Weights on Baidu only; University-1652 is research use only.

name: GSDC 10th place solution
summary: 10th-place solution for the Kaggle Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge.
why_it_matters: Readable Kaggle-style pipeline for smartphone GNSS post-processing.
hackathon_notes: Apache-2.0 code; GSDC data is under Kaggle competition rules (not checked). Denoises host-baseline positions (STFT + CNN, LightGBM on IMU) and snaps to training ground truth with KNN, so it relies on repeated routes. Private score about 2.61 m.

name: Smartphone Decimeter Challenge MATLAB package
summary: MATLAB package from an ION GNSS+ 2021 decimeter challenge entry.
why_it_matters: MATLAB route for smartphone GNSS positioning.
hackathon_notes: Reference only: the EKF, INS and magnitude submodules are private, so it does not run as cloned. MIT. From an ENAC master's thesis.

name: ML GNSS/IMU integration (GSDC 2022)
summary: GSDC 2022 pipeline: an ML classifier picks the drive environment (highway, tree-lined, downtown) to set rtklib-py PPK options, then a loosely coupled GNSS/IMU Kalman filter refines the result.
why_it_matters: Example of learned GNSS/IMU fusion on phone data.
hackathon_notes: Reference. No licence (all rights reserved).

name: Google SDC corrections (Swift Navigation)
summary: SSR and OSR GNSS correction data for the 2021 Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge drives, in SBP, JSON, RTCM3 and RINEX.
why_it_matters: Real correction streams aligned to a public phone dataset - good for practising RTK/PPP on phones.
hackathon_notes: No licence; Swift provides it as is. 2020 drives have OSR but no or partial SSR; 2021 drives have both. Pair with GSDC 2021 data and RTKLIB.

name: MAINS
summary: Magnetic-field aided inertial navigation system for indoor positioning, compared against a magnetic EKF.
why_it_matters: Magnetic field anomalies as a GNSS-free position aid indoors.
hackathon_notes: MATLAB with eight recorded datasets in data/. Clone with --recurse-submodules (MAINS is a submodule). MAINS code is GPL-3.0, MAGEKF Apache-2.0. Test on your own magnetometer arrays.

name: Magnetic-field odometry
summary: MATLAB simulation of a tightly-integrated magnetic-field aided INS using a magnetometer array; it generates its own trajectory and sensor data.
why_it_matters: Shows magnetometer arrays as odometry where cameras fail.
hackathon_notes: MATLAB simulation only, no real data. GPL-3.0.

name: ScalLoc
summary: Continuous geo-localization of oblique thermal UAV sequences against a 2D satellite map (VGGT reconstruction + MINIMA-RoMa matching), with the Thermal-Oblique dataset: 216 trajectories, 28,112 frames.
why_it_matters: Night-time thermal geo-localization with oblique cameras, closer to real FPV/ISR views.
hackathon_notes: No code licence yet - the author's notice says it is pending (all rights reserved). Depends on VGGT, whose licence prohibits military and warfare use; the original VGGT-1B checkpoint is non-commercial. Data, map and weights are on HF (gated, Apache-2.0 tag).

name: MBZIRC Maritime Grand Challenge simulator
summary: Simulator (Ignition Fortress + ROS 2) for the MBZIRC Maritime Grand Challenge where UAVs and USVs cooperate in a GNSS-denied environment.
why_it_matters: Ready-made maritime GNSS-denied multi-vehicle scenario.
hackathon_notes: Built for Ubuntu 20.04, ROS 2 Galactic and Ignition Fortress, all now end of life; use the osrf/mbzirc Docker image (needs nvidia-docker2). Apache-2.0.

name: Race Against the Machine dataset
summary: Annotated dataset of fast autonomous and human-piloted quadrotor flight with visual, inertial and mocap data plus labelled racing gates, from TII.
why_it_matters: High-speed VIO and gate-relative state estimation data.
hackathon_notes: Dataset CC BY 4.0, code MIT. 18 autonomous and 18 piloted flights per README, over 21 m/s with mocap ground truth; v3.0.0 (Oct 2025) adds six pro-pilot flights. Use to test VIO at high speed.

name: Swarm in Blocks
summary: Block-programming and web control platform for drone swarms on COEX Clover (ROS, Gazebo); CopterHack 2022 winner by team Atena. The repo now holds Swarm in Blocks 2.0 (CopterHack 2023, 4th).
why_it_matters: Example of a winning open CopterHack project.
hackathon_notes: No licence (all rights reserved). Runs on the Clover Gazebo simulation; the real-swarm mode is barely tested.

name: Clover Rescue Project
summary: Main web server and client (Node.js, Socket.IO) of the Clover Rescue Team's CopterHack 2022 project, 3rd place; the drone-side server is DevMBS/CRTClover.
why_it_matters: Example finalist code.
hackathon_notes: MIT. Reference only.
